result.summary: A narrow, one-way residential street with continuous sidewalks on both sides and row houses built directly to the property line. Parallel parking on both sides provides a physical buffer for pedestrians but creates significant visual obstructions for anyone attempting to cross the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Continuous rows of parked vehicles on both sides of the narrow street block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians who might step into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block

hazards.name: Sidewalk debris
hazards.description: Trash bags and bins are placed on the sidewalk, slightly narrowing the effective walking width.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the nearest intersections to improve visibility and shorten the crossing distance for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Planting street trees would provide shade and create a vertical sense of enclosure that naturally encourages slower driving speeds.

interventions.title: Speed Cushions
interventions.description: Install mid-block speed cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low on this residential corridor.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide but poorly maintained sidewalk with significant physical obstructions, including a utility pole and a trash bin. The lack of a buffer between the walkway and the narrow roadway, combined with a driveway crossing, creates a low-quality environment for walking.

hazards.name: Utility pole obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility pole is situated in the middle of the sidewalk, significantly narrowing the effective walking width and creating a collision hazard.

hazards.name: Poor pavement condition
hazards.description: The sidewalk surface is cracked with weeds growing through, creating potential trip hazards.

hazards.name: Driveway conflict point
hazards.description: A garage entrance crosses the sidewalk, creating a point of potential conflict between pedestrians and vehicles.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair
interventions.description: Resurface the sidewalk to eliminate trip hazards and improve accessibility.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate the utility pole to the edge of the sidewalk or into a furniture zone to provide a clear walking path.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and the roadway.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban street with parallel parking on both sides and buildings situated directly at the sidewalk edge. Pedestrian infrastructure is minimal, consisting of narrow sidewalks with occasional obstructions like utility poles and no visible marked crossings or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the narrow street significantly blocks sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the foreground and midground

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are placed directly in the narrow sidewalk path, reducing effective width and creating obstacles for those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, midground

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: The intersection ahead lacks visible crosswalk markings or curb ramps, providing no designated or protected space for pedestrians to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and bring pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond the parked cars.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Paint high-visibility continental-style crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove the parking spaces closest to the intersection to ensure clear sight triangles for both drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a typical residential street with a continuous, well-maintained sidewalk and parallel on-street parking. While the pedestrian path is clear, the lack of a physical buffer from traffic and the visual obstruction caused by parked vehicles are notable characteristics.

hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb line create a visual barrier between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway, which can be hazardous if a pedestrian attempts to cross mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and right side of the image along the curb.
